title: Jǫrmungandr, spelled the way the sources wrote it

body:
# Jǫrmungandr, spelled the way the sources wrote it
There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *jormungandr*. This is the file on how **Jǫrmungandr** replaced it.

Jǫrmungandr is one of the three great threats to the gods, alongside Fenrir and Hel. It does not speak in the myths, yet its body defines the shape of the world and its final battle with Þórr is one of the climactic moments of Ragnarök. When the gods learned that Loki and Angrboða had produced three monstrous children — Fenrir, Jǫrmungandr, and Hel — they seized them.  Fenrir they bound, Hel they cast into Niflhel, and Jǫrmungandr they threw into the sea that surrounds all lands.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Jǫrmungandr
- **ASCII form:** jormungandr
- **Meaning:** "Huge monster (from jǫrmun + gandr)"
- **Domain of influence:** World Serpent
- **Pantheon:** Norse
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** ᛁᚢᚱᛘᚢᚾᚴᛅᚾᛏᚱ
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 124 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

**Jǫrmungandr** preserves its form without added diacritics: the restoration here is the exactness of the spelling itself, the form the tradition's own sources record. *jormungandr* and **Jǫrmungandr** may look interchangeable to a search box; they are not interchangeable to a philologist.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Jǫrmungandr** lives at [/sites/jormungandr/](/sites/jormungandr/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/jormungandr/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/jormungandr/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/jormungandr/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Jǫrmungandr** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Gaming, Fantasy & Entertainment IP** — The world serpent; God of War’s most memorable co-star.
- **Mapping & Geospatial** — Its coil defines the shape of the world; the coastline as one endless body.
- **Cybersecurity & Digital Protection** — The boundary that holds the world together — perimeter defense with teeth.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Norse tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Poetic Edda](/texts/poetic-edda/) and [Prose Edda](/texts/prose-edda/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/jormungandr/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.
